+﻿# Current submission package: evidence-constrained mixed-halide methodology study
+
+This directory is the submission root for the current manuscript only.
+
+## Scope lock
+
+- Study type: provenance-preserving materials-informatics methodology study.
+- Primary model layer: 37 locked development rows from 30 DOI groups.
+- Formal provenance/context pool: 120 DOI groups, plus 10 reserve DOI groups.
+- Locked external cohort: 4 DOI groups.
+- Phase 879 context-burden layer: 55 DOI groups, 158 evidence windows, 280 direct PCE values.
+- Phase 885 focused pair signals: 7 retained as context-only; 0 prediction-eligible after reconciliation.
+
+## Contents
+
+- `manuscript/`: current polished manuscript candidate.
+- `figures/`: rendered Figure 7.
+- `figure_sources/`: Figure 7 data, plotting code, traceability, and execution QA.
+- `audit/`: model, context burden, reconciliation, claim, risk, and terminology records.
+- `metadata/`: public package metadata and checksums.
+
+## Explicit exclusion
+
+The older 38,442-device-record study is not part of this public release. Author metadata, cover letter, submission checklist, and copyrighted source PDFs/SI are intentionally excluded.
+
+## Reproducibility boundary
+
+Copyrighted source PDFs/SI are not redistributed here. Derived evidence metadata, source locators, scripts, summaries, and checksums are included or referenced by the audit files. Final repository release and DOI claims require actual verification after upload.
+
+

+﻿from pathlib import Path
+import csv
+
+INPUT = Path(__file__).with_name("Figure7_data.csv")
+OUTPUT = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "figures" / "Figure7_reproducibility_rerender.png"
+
+
+def load_rows():
+    with INPUT.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as handle:
+        return list(csv.DictReader(handle))
+
+
+def build_figure():
+    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+
+    rows = load_rows()
+    burden = [r for r in rows if r["panel"] == "A"]
+    promotion = [r for r in rows if r["panel"] == "B"]
+    labels = ["High", "Moderate", "Low"]
+    counts = [int(r["count"]) for r in burden]
+    colors = ["#B2182B", "#EF8A62", "#67A9CF"]
+
+    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8.2, 3.4), constrained_layout=True)
+    axes[0].bar(labels, counts, color=colors, edgecolor="#222222", linewidth=0.6)
+    axes[0].set_ylabel("DOI groups")
+    axes[0].set_title("A  Context-compression burden")
+    axes[0].set_ylim(0, max(counts) + 6)
+    axes[0].set_xlabel("Compression-burden category")
+    for index, count in enumerate(counts):
+        axes[0].text(index, count + 0.7, str(count), ha="center", va="bottom")
+
+    labels_b = ["Pair signals", "Prediction-eligible"]
+    counts_b = [int(promotion[0]["count"]), int(promotion[1]["count"])]
+    axes[1].bar(labels_b, counts_b, color=["#2166AC", "#F4A582"], edgecolor="#222222", linewidth=0.6)
+    axes[1].set_ylabel("Records")
+    axes[1].set_title("B  Promotion boundary")
+    axes[1].set_ylim(0, 8)
+    axes[1].set_xlabel("Reconciliation status")
+    for index, count in enumerate(counts_b):
+        axes[1].text(index, count + 0.2, str(count), ha="center", va="bottom")
+
+    fig.savefig(OUTPUT, dpi=300)
+    return OUTPUT
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    build_figure()
+

@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@
+﻿# Evidence-constrained prediction of intervention-associated PCE gains in mixed-halide perovskites
+
+**Peng Xiangkai** and **Aung Ko Ko KYAW**\\
+Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China\\
+Corresponding author: Aung Ko Ko KYAW (aung@sustech.edu.cn)
+
+## Abstract
+
+Literature-derived materials datasets often combine paired device comparisons with heterogeneous device contexts, incomplete descriptors, and source-specific performance statistics. We developed an evidence-constrained workflow for representing intervention-associated changes in power conversion efficiency (PCE) while preserving source provenance and publication-group independence. The primary development matrix contained 37 rows from 30 DOI groups. We defined the estimand as the source-native target-minus-reference PCE difference and evaluated a predeclared Ridge model with leave-one-DOI-out validation. In internal validation, the locked Ridge model did not outperform the global mean baseline (DOI-balanced mean absolute error, 1.439 versus 1.256 percentage points), so no algorithmic-superiority claim is made. A locked one-shot external summary across four DOI groups supplied bounded transportability evidence: the Ridge error was lower than the global baseline for three groups, and all four prediction intervals covered the observed effects. Exploratory context extraction retained 35 directly reported contexts across ten additional candidates, including multiple arms, doses, scan directions, and source-native statistics; 26 contexts contained complete paired numeric PCE values. These contexts were not pooled into the primary model. The resulting framework treats evidence quality, uncertainty, applicability domain, and failure boundaries as part of the computational result. Additional stress tests showed that DOI-level pooling changed the descriptive effect distribution, random row-level splitting produced a lower apparent error than DOI-grouped splitting, and a simple abstention rule reduced retained-case error in a small external set. These analyses support an auditable transportability workflow rather than a causal estimator or universal predictor.
+
+## Introduction
+
+Mixed-halide perovskites offer a useful setting for materials informatics because device performance is shaped by composition, processing, interfaces, and measurement context. Prior mixed-halide studies report phase segregation, recovery, vacancy healing, and additive or interface interventions in source-specific device contexts [ref_21acsenergylett8b0_p654001; ref_21acsenergylett3c0_p654002; ref_02solr2022099_p654013]. However, literature comparisons are not automatically interchangeable. A reported efficiency may describe a champion device, an average over devices, a forward or reverse scan, or a particular treatment dose. Comparable heterogeneity is visible across interface, additive, crystallization, and transport-layer studies in the local evidence set [ref_16jcej2021129247_p654022; ref_16jcej2020124903_p654018; ref_16jjmat202209005_p654011; ref_16jjmst202005073_p654019]. Comparator identity may also be ambiguous when a source reports several interventions or device architectures. Treating every reported number as an independent and identically defined observation can create leakage, obscure uncertainty, and produce apparently precise but poorly transportable models.
+
+Here we develop an evidence-constrained paired-effect workflow for mixed-halide perovskite interventions. The central design choice is to represent a source-native target-minus-reference PCE effect while keeping DOI groups as the unit of independence. Evidence that cannot be safely compressed into a unique confirmatory estimand is retained in explicitly exploratory or audit layers rather than silently discarded. Descriptor labels are similarly bounded by direct evidence and are not interpreted as causal mechanisms when the source does not support that interpretation.
+
+The contribution is therefore methodological and deployment-oriented. We combine provenance-preserving source/SI pairing, isolated eligibility and arm-binding review, DOI-grouped validation, a locked regularized model, applicability-domain auditing, and context-level exploratory summaries. The source bibliography and citation keys are provided in the accompanying machine-readable reference package. The goal is not to claim universal prediction. It is to test whether a transparent workflow can connect heterogeneous literature evidence to bounded transportability statements while making failure regimes visible.
+
+## Results
+
+### Evidence-constrained data model
+
+The development matrix contained 37 rows from 30 DOI groups. The confirmatory estimand was defined as target PCE minus reference PCE within a source-native paired device context. Repeated rows from the same DOI were not treated as independent validation groups. Eligibility, arm identity, mixed-halide scope, device scope, and descriptors were recorded through staged, outcome-blinded review where applicable. Unresolved or multi-context records were preserved with their unresolved status.
+
+The evidence utility policy separated the primary model layer from sensitivity, exploratory, and audit uses. This separation allowed heterogeneous records to contribute information about missingness, context variation, and failure boundaries without changing the locked model or introducing outcome-driven comparator selection.
+
+### DOI-grouped internal validation
+
+The predeclared primary model was a Ridge model with alpha equal to 10.0 evaluated using leave-one-DOI-out validation. The locked primary Ridge model produced a DOI-balanced mean absolute error of 1.439 percentage points, compared with 1.256 percentage points for the global mean baseline. The primary model therefore did not establish algorithmic superiority. A mechanism-ablated Ridge analysis had lower development error, but it was exploratory and did not replace the predeclared primary model.
+
+This negative result is retained as a central finding. It indicates that the current evidence and descriptor coverage support an auditable workflow and bounded deployment analysis, but do not justify presenting the model as a universally accurate predictor.
+
+### External transportability and applicability boundaries
+
+The locked model was applied once to an external cohort of four DOI groups without changing the model, alpha, feature set, or applicability threshold. Ridge absolute error was lower than the global baseline for three of four DOI groups. All four prediction intervals covered their observed paired effects. Because the external cohort contains only four DOI groups, these results are treated as supportive transportability evidence rather than calibration proof or statistically established superiority.
+
+The external cohort included both within-domain and outside-domain cases. The outside-domain case was not removed after observing its outcome. It is retained as a deployment-boundary observation: an outside-domain prediction can occasionally have lower error than a baseline, but that single observation does not establish robustness beyond the predeclared domain.
+
+### Exploratory context heterogeneity
+
+A batch exploratory extraction retained 35 directly reported contexts across ten candidate papers. Multiple arms, doses, scan directions, champion or average statistics, and source-native context labels were kept as separate records. Twenty-six contexts contained complete paired numeric PCE values; nine records remained incomplete for paired numerical analysis. Across the 26 numeric contexts, the mean context-specific delta PCE was 2.227 percentage points, the median was 2.15, and the observed range was 0 to 7.27 percentage points. These descriptive summaries are not pooled causal estimates and were not promoted into the primary model. Their purpose is to quantify how much information is lost when heterogeneous literature contexts are compressed into a single number.
+
+## Context-preservation stress test
+
+To test whether context preservation changes the empirical signal rather than merely documenting it, we compared three representations built from the existing frozen records. The context-aware representation retained 26 complete paired contexts across 10 DOI groups. A naive DOI-pooled representation first averaged all complete contexts within each DOI, leaving 10 DOI-level records. The locked confirmatory development matrix contained 37 rows from 30 DOI groups. The context-aware records had a mean delta PCE of 2.227 percentage points (median 2.15; range 0.00–7.27), whereas DOI pooling shifted the mean to 2.439 percentage points (median 2.07; range 1.16–5.69). These are descriptive representation contrasts, not alternative primary estimates.
+The expanded context-first audit quantified the scale of estimand compression in the literature evidence layer. Across 55 DOI groups represented in 158 high-priority evidence windows, 280 direct PCE values were retained without selecting a single value per publication. Twenty-three DOI groups were classified as high compression burden, 26 as moderate, and 6 as low. A focused review of seven direct PCE pair signals found that none could be promoted after independent Reviewer B/C reconciliation because the available evidence did not uniquely establish the full target/reference/statistic estimand. These records were therefore retained as exploratory context-only evidence rather than added to the predictive matrix (Figure 7).
+
+
+## Publication-group leakage benchmark
+
+Using the same Ridge pipeline and alpha=10, repeated random row-level five-fold splitting produced a mean MAE of 1.179 ± 0.101, whereas DOI-grouped five-fold splitting produced 1.329 ± 0.000. The lower row-level error is consistent with optimistic leakage when related contexts from the same publication can occur in both training and test folds. We therefore retain DOI-grouped leave-one-DOI-out validation as the primary estimate of generalization. This benchmark is diagnostic and is not used to claim that the grouped model is intrinsically more accurate.
+
+## Prediction with abstention
+
+For the four locked external predictions, always predicting gave an MAE of 0.942 percentage points. A descriptive policy that retained only cases inside the applicability domain and below the median external interval width retained 1 of 4 cases (0.25 coverage) and gave a retained-case MAE of 0.602; no retained case had an absolute error ≤0.5 percentage points, compared with 0.25 under always-predict. Because this analysis uses only four external cases and the interval threshold is descriptive, it demonstrates selective-risk behavior rather than calibrated decision utility.
+
+## Discussion
+
+The main result is a workflow-level contribution: evidence constraints and deployment boundaries can be represented as analytical outputs rather than treated as preprocessing noise. The negative internal comparison prevents an inflated model-performance narrative, while the external cohort provides a bounded test of transportability. The exploratory layer further shows that records rejected from confirmatory scoring can remain scientifically useful when each context is preserved and labeled.
+
+This structure is relevant to materials informatics settings in which the limiting factor is not only sample count but also comparability. A larger table assembled without DOI grouping, arm provenance, statistic-context labels, and domain auditing could generate a more impressive apparent sample size while weakening the interpretation. Conversely, strict primary gating need not imply that all ambiguous evidence is useless. The two-layer design makes that distinction explicit.
+
+The descriptor and mechanism layers should be interpreted as evidence-bounded annotations. For example, an interface or energy-alignment label records directly supported evidence categories; it does not prove a microscopic mechanism or establish that an intervention caused the observed PCE difference. This distinction is essential when integrating heterogeneous reports into computational models.
+
+
+The added stress tests make the workflow contribution empirical. Context compression changed the descriptive effect distribution, while row-level splitting produced a lower apparent error than publication-group splitting. This pattern is consistent with a familiar but often hidden risk in literature-derived materials datasets: observations that appear numerically distinct may still share publication-level preparation, device, and measurement context. Treating DOI groups as the unit of independence therefore functions as a transportability safeguard rather than a cosmetic data-management choice.
+
+The abstention analysis provides a complementary deployment perspective. In a small external set, refusing to make high-uncertainty or out-of-domain predictions reduced the error among retained predictions, at the cost of low coverage. We interpret this as evidence that abstention and applicability-domain reporting can be useful outputs when sample size is limited—not as proof of calibrated uncertainty or universal screening utility.
+
+## Limitations
+
+First, the external cohort remains small, so the abstention analysis is a bounded selective-risk demonstration rather than a calibration study. Transportability evidence remains limited and calibration cannot be established. Second, the literature contains heterogeneous device architectures, processing routes, measurement statistics, and missing descriptors. Third, the primary model uses one target endpoint, paired-PCE, and a relatively small development matrix. Fourth, unresolved contexts cannot support a unique confirmatory effect without additional prespecification or source-native information. Fifth, the workflow does not identify causal effects and does not replace prospective experiments. Finally, the added leakage and abstention benchmarks are diagnostic analyses with small effective sample sizes; they do not establish universal performance or decision utility. The rendered figures and manuscript package remain subject to author review and journal-format checks.
+
+## Conclusion
+
+We present an evidence-constrained, provenance-preserving workflow for modeling intervention-associated PCE differences in mixed-halide perovskites. DOI-grouped validation, one-shot external scoring, applicability-domain auditing, and context-level exploratory retention jointly support a conservative but useful computational materials result. The strongest conclusion is not universal prediction; it is that a transparent workflow can expose where literature-derived paired effects are transportable, where uncertainty is substantial, and where context heterogeneity prevents safe compression.
+
+## Data and code availability
+
+The analysis is accompanied by frozen input manifests, executable local scripts, reviewer-audit records, generated figure sources, machine-readable derived data, and SHA-256 checksums. The analysis code, derived figure-source data, and documentation are archived at GitHub (https://github.com/pengxiangkai1/mixed-halide-pce-evidence-constrained), release v1.0.1, and Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21908297). Copyrighted source PDFs, supplementary information files, and private reviewer materials are not included in the public archive.
+
+
+## Author contributions
+
+Peng Xiangkai: Conceptualization, Methodology, Software, Validation, Formal analysis, Investigation, Data curation, Writing - original draft, Writing - review & editing, and Visualization. Aung Ko Ko KYAW: Conceptualization, Methodology, Supervision, and Writing - review & editing.
+
+## Graphical abstract
+
+The graphical abstract summarizes the evidence-constrained workflow from heterogeneous literature evidence through target/reference arm binding and DOI-grouped modeling to auditable effect, uncertainty, applicability-domain, and failure-boundary outputs.
+
+
+
